answer: Storage proof: a node commits a Merkle root over its shard; each epoch the chain samples leaves from entropy in the prior header, spreading them like a nebula of independent draws no one can predict early. The node must return each leaf with its audit path in one block, and fetching bytes from a remote peer misses that deadline, so only holding the data is cheap. A missed opening burns a quartz-hard bond larger than a full epoch of emission, so partial storage is negative-expectation. Each shard grows from its own grove of account keys; one operator cannot cover many identities with one copy.
